overview: Carbis Bay is a large family beach just around the corner from St Ives, tucked into its own little bay between Porthminster Point and Hawk’s Point. With lifeguards in season and a car park, toilets and cafés close by, it’s about as easy as a beach day gets.
It made world news in 2021 as the venue for the G7 summit, held at the hotel on the seafront.

expect.title: Family beach
expect.text: A wide sandy beach in its own bay, popular with families.

expect.title: Coast path
expect.text: The South West Coast Path runs above the beach, so you can walk the mile or so into St Ives along the coast.

expect.title: By train
expect.text: Carbis Bay has its own railway station right above the beach, on the scenic St Ives branch line.

goodToKnow.label: Getting there
goodToKnow.text: About a mile from St Ives. The station above the beach is on the line from St Erth, where you change for mainline trains.

week.text: A great choice if you’re staying around St Ives and want something easier than the town’s busy beaches. It faces north-east, so it’s sheltered from westerly winds. You could park here and take the train or walk the coast path into St Ives instead of battling for parking in town.

pairWith.why: St Ives’ big sandy town beach, over the point
a huge quiet beach towards the Hayle estuary
the gallery in St Ives for a wet hour

tips: Take the little branch-line train into St Ives: it’s one stop and saves the parking hassle.
